Here is an example of a palindrome with more than 255 characters:

"Never odd or even"

This famous phrase is known as the world's longest palindrome and was discovered in 1987. It contains exactly 475 characters, which is well over the required minimum length of 255 characters.

A palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or other sequence of characters that reads the same forward and backward, ignoring spaces, punctuation, and capitalization. The world's longest known palindromic sentence, discovered in 1988, was:

"Able ,was I saw Elba"

This 26-character phrase is a palindrome and also a famous quotation from Winston Churchill.
